why: Quote verified verbatim at plugins/org.md#seed-containers-and-ci (was line 635 of the retired plugin-marketplaces page) (two-sentence line, second half does not reverse it). The narrow identifier half is true: no CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_SEED_DIR / layered read-only seed directory exists. But the finding is refuted on both its evidence and its consequence. (1) EVIDENCE FALSE AS STATED: the claim says all five names 'return zero hits under --include=*.ts repo-wide'. PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR returns 5 hits -- packages/shared/src/workspaces/paths.ts:11 and :99, workspaces/index.ts:46, plus two in __tests__/paths.test.ts. Bare-name grep collision with a real managed-cache-root constant; the sweep never re-ran its own command. (2) CONSEQUENCE FALSE for the variable the finding singles out as mattering: KEEP_MARKETPLACE_ON_FAILURE is an OPT-IN in Claude Code to stop it deleting and re-cloning a marketplace whose background pull failed. Our fork does the non-destructive thing UNCONDITIONALLY, by design. packages/shared/src/marketplace/registry-source.ts mergeFailedFetch keeps the previous catalog under the failed fetch's signature and explicitly refuses to delete the on-disk copy ('after a failed refresh it is the only surviving copy, and removing it turns a recoverable state into an unrecoverable one'), citing the same bug one subsystem over from mcp.md. upgrade() (:857-870) on a non-persistable fetch leaves the row and its signature untouched and returns typed fetch-failed / fetch-timeout, 'so the catalog the user can still browse stays the catalog an install resolves against'. There is no destructive default here to need an escape hatch from -- the airgap resilience the page sells via the flag is our floor, not our gap. (3) PREFER_HTTPS likewise: packages/shared/src/plugins/source-resolver.ts:115-116 -- 'Claude clones shorthand over SSH by default (:553); we resolve to the HTTPS repository URL because codeload is the acquisition route this app has.' The flag's effect is our unconditional default. (4) GIT_TIMEOUT_MS is not absent as a concept: REGISTRY_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 45_000 (registry-source.ts:54) with an options.fetchTimeoutMs override (:323) and a distinct 'fetch-timeout' upgrade reason -- configurable, just not env-driven. (5) The seed directory's container/CI intent is served by a deliberate product difference, not left open: admin pre-provisioning arrives through server-delivered managed settings (packages/shared/src/config/managed-delivery.ts, gateway /api/v1/cli/managed-settings) as extraKnownMarketplaces, registered idempotently by PluginRegistrySource.ensureDeliveredMarketplaces() (:341-378) under the same strictKnownMarketplaces allowlist an interactive add passes, with catalogs cached to disk. This fork delivers policy through its corporate gateway rather than through container env vars. Not one of the nine owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (checked; none touches marketplaces or seeding).
correctedState: No CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_* environment variable is honoured, and there is no layered read-only seed directory: a container image cannot point Nessy at a pre-populated plugins tree via env var. That is the whole of the true gap, and it is narrower than the finding claims. The finding's grep is wrong -- PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR has 5 hits under --include='*.ts' (packages/shared/src/workspaces/paths.ts:11,:99; workspaces/index.ts:46; two tests) as the managed cache-root constant. More importantly the three behaviours the flags buy are already our unconditional defaults, so their absence is not a gap: keep-marketplace-on-failure is default and non-optional (registry-source.ts mergeFailedFetch keeps the last resolved catalog and never deletes the on-disk copy; upgrade() leaves the row unstamped on fetch-failed/fetch-timeout so browse and install keep resolving against it), HTTPS-for-owner/repo-shorthand is default (source-resolver.ts:115-116, deliberately diverging from Claude's SSH default), and the git fetch timeout is configurable in-code (REGISTRY_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS 45s, options.fetchTimeoutMs). The container/CI pre-provisioning use case is met by a different, gateway-shaped mechanism: extraKnownMarketplaces in server-delivered managed settings, registered by ensureDeliveredMarketplaces() behind the strictKnownMarketplaces allowlist. Any residual work is 'expose a seed path for air-gapped images', not 'restore a missing offline escape hatch'.
